items.period: Shuowen small-seal style; modern redraw, not a dated specimen
items.tradition: Small seal-script style, rendered as a modern vector
items.caption: This small-seal-style redraw shows a curved inner form within a larger enclosing outline. Shuowen interpreted it as an unborn child within a pregnant figure; the redraw illustrates that received-form interpretation, not the graph’s earliest origin.
items.alt: Black small-seal-style form with a curved shape inside a larger enclosing outline.
items.selection_reason: The image makes the inner-and-outer arrangement behind Shuowen’s pregnancy interpretation visible. Its script-style label does not establish a dated specimen.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, as stated on the Commons file page.

limitations.text: The earliest form of 包 remains unresolved. Shuowen’s pregnancy interpretation and the proposal that 包 developed from a graph depicting someone holding a child are competing accounts; this redraw does not establish an ancient form sequence.
The received-form pregnancy interpretation and the transmitted wrapping use are both documented, but their historical relationship has not been established.
